one_line: single-file SMART on FHIR growth-monitoring app for the Epic sandbox
skills: LLM prompt design for clinical summaries
tools: HAPI FHIR (public and self-hosted, in the Codex variant)
data: Epic FHIR sandbox (Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest, Condition)
WHO boys height reference 0-24 months (embedded p3/p50/p97)
CDC boys height reference 2-10 years (embedded p3/p50/p97)
Ranke 1983 Turner syndrome girls height reference (Codex variant)
synthetic demo patients loaded as a FHIR transaction bundle

decisions.chose: a public HAPI FHIR server with a patient dropdown, in the follow-on build
decisions.over: the Epic sandbox launch with OAuth and PKCE
decisions.because: the demo needed its own teaching vignettes, which a fixed sandbox roster cannot supply, and the growth logic is unchanged either way
decisions.evidence: Replace Epic sandbox with HAPI FHIR public server. ... Remove all OAuth/PKCE code. Replace the "Connect to Epic Sandbox" flow with a patient selector dropdown that lists the three demo patients by name.

decisions.chose: demo cases built around trajectory, velocity, and delayed recognition
decisions.over: vignettes built on population or ethnicity-specific expected growth
decisions.because: a subgroup-specific chart can make a remediable problem look typical and talk a clinician out of a real concern
decisions.evidence: Condition-specific references can help interpretation, but they should not override clinical concern or normalize remediable pathology.

decisions.chose: keeping the existing percentile tables, interpolation, and anomaly rules untouched while adding features
decisions.over: rewriting the growth engine during the feature build
decisions.because: the clinical logic was the part that had already been checked, so it was fenced off from the rebuild
decisions.evidence: Do not change ... WHO/CDC percentile tables and interpolation logic ... detectAnomalies() function logic

decisions.chose: asking for the model API key at run time and holding it in sessionStorage
decisions.over: a committed or gitignored config file holding the key
decisions.because: the app is served as static files, so anything in the repo ships with it

decisions.chose: self-hosted HAPI as the custom-data lane, with Epic kept as the interoperability lane
decisions.over: treating the HAPI work as a throwaway detour
decisions.because: the growth-processing logic stays the same and only the read source changes
decisions.evidence: That means the HAPI work is not throwaway. It becomes your custom demo-data lane, while Epic becomes your interoperability lane.

broke.what: the first scopes requested were the user-level ones, which do not return a patient context; they had to be switched to patient-level and the granted scopes printed to debug it
the sandbox patient came back with no vitals at all, so the chart had nothing to draw and synthetic pediatric measurements were added as a fallback
broke.evidence: // sandbox patient has no vitals -- use synthetic pediatric data for demo

broke.what: the plain category search for vital signs did not work; the query had to carry the full terminology system URI
requests needed an explicit FHIR JSON Accept header before the patient fetch behaved
switching between demo patients and plotting the parental target line were both wrong and had to be fixed after the feature build
broke.evidence: Fix patient switching and parental target plotting

question: Can a lightweight browser app read a child's growth history straight from a health record and surface faltering that a short visit would miss?
rejected_line: dropped the Epic OAuth/PKCE launch in the follow-on build for a HAPI server with a patient dropdown, because the teaching vignettes had to be ones I could author and load myself
